newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy committee fails to agree TV bill amendment.
newsitem.headline: Italy committee fails to agree TV bill amendment.

text.p: Italian political parties failed to reach agreement on part of a draft law on reforming Italy's broadcasting and telecommunications sector, parliamentary sources said.

The bill contains legislation to set up a watchdog for the telecommunications sector, a measure which is a prerequisite for the privatisation of Italian state telecoms giant Stet, expected in the second half of this year.
The bill, which has been delayed for months by parliamentary filibustering, is currently being examined by a Senate (upper house) committee.

Without this agreement it is likely to face thousands of amendments when it goes to the full chamber of the Senate, meaning the government could be forced to call a confidence vote to push it through.
Senate sources said the draft law, which also contains antitrust rules for the television sector, would now go directly to the Senate's full chamber where it is timetabled to be examined from May 13.

Committee members from the centre-left government coalition and the opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance, which is led by broadcasting tycoon Silvio Berlusconi, had failed to agree over an amendment to the bill relating to pay-TV. (( --Rome bureau +39 6 6782501 ))
